artworks.title: Hermaphroditus and Salmacis
artworks.description: Louvre relief from the Albani collection: Salmacis coils around Hermaphroditus at the fountain — Ovid's Carian nymph frozen in marble embrace.

artworks.title: Landscape with Salmacis and Hermaphroditus
artworks.description: Lagrenée's pastoral landscape nests the fountain encounter in soft trees and water — Salmacis as Rococo desire before the waters fuse the pair.

artworks.title: Salmacis and Hermaphroditus
artworks.description: Rowlandson's watercolour: the nymph clinging at the spring — English Regency wit applied to Ovid's most intimate metamorphosis.

artworks.title: Dish with Hermaphroditus and the Nymph Salmacis
artworks.description: Xanto's maiolica dish: Salmacis and Hermaphroditus as table spectacle — Renaissance Urbino ceramics keeping the fountain myth in bright glaze.

artworks.title: Nymph of Salmacis
artworks.description: Bunny's fin-de-siècle Salmacis alone — the Carian naiad as Symbolist water spirit, desire before the embrace.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Book IV — Salmacis will not let go, and the fountain fuses nymph and youth forever.

popCulture.title: Salmacis
popCulture.description: The Carian naiad whose spring still names the embrace that joined her to Hermaphroditus.
